GENERAL ACCIDENTAL RELEASE PREVENTION PROGRAM  
The following is a summary of the accident prevention program in place for the storage of the railcars disconnected from a motive force at the facility. This summary describes the management system in place to implement the accident prevention program. During storage, the railcars are regulated by the EPA's RMP regulation and is not subject to the OSHA PSM standard.  

Prevention Program (Program 2 Elements)
The following is a summary of the accident prevention program in place for the process at the facility.

Safety Information:
MPLX keeps a variety of technical documents that are used to help maintain safe operation of the processes. These documents address chemical properties and associated hazards, limits for key process parameters and specific chemical inventories, and equipment design basis/configuration information. The reference documents are kept electronically and on file at the facility to provide open access to employees.  

The rail cars are DOT containers and designed and operated in accordance with DOT regulations.

 

Hazard Review:
MPLX has a comprehensive program to help ensure that hazards associated with the process are identified and controlled. Within this program, each process is systematically examined to identify hazards and ensure that adequate controls are in place to manage these hazards.?? 
MPLX will use one or more of the following techniques to identify hazards: what-if, checklist, what-if/checklist, hazard and operability (HAZOP), failure mode and effects analysis (FMEA), or fault tree analysis (FTA). HAZOP analysis is recognized as one of the most systematic and thorough hazard evaluation techniques and will be utilized for each major process change or renovation. The analyses are conducted using a team of people who have operating and maintenance experience as well as engineering expertise. This team identifies and evaluates hazards of the process as well as accident prevention and mi

tigation measures, and the team makes suggestions for additional prevention and/or mitigation measures when the team believes such measures are necessary.?? 
Each PHA will address the following:?? 
1) hazards of the process,?? 
2) previous incidents with likely potential for catastrophic consequences,?? 
3) consequences of failure of engineering and administrative controls,?? 
4) Engineering and administrative control applicable to the hazards and their inter-relationships,?? 
5) facility sitting issues, and?? 
6) human factors.?? 
The PHA team findings are compiled in a written report and are forwarded to local and corporate management for resolution. Implementation of mitigation options in response to PHA findings is based on a relative risk ranking assigned by the PHA team. This ranking helps ensure that potential accident scenarios assigned the highest risk receive immediate attention. Approved mitigation options in response to PHA team findings are tracked until they are completed. The final resolution of each finding is documented and retained.?? 
To help ensure that the process controls and/or process hazards do not eventually deviate significantly from the original design safety features, the facility periodically updates and revalidates the hazard analysis results. These periodic reviews are conducted at least every five years and will be conducted at this frequency until the process is no longer operative. The results and findings from these updates are documented and retained. Once again, the team findings are forwarded to management for consideration, and the final resolution of the findings is documented and retained.??
The most recent Verne Hazard Review was completed on 2/2/2023.

Operating Procedures
 MPLX maintains written procedures that address various modes of operations. These procedures include activities such as loading products, rail car switching, operation of combustor system, and operation of the air system during which time the facility i

s subject to Department of Transportation (DOT).  These procedures can be used as a reference by experienced operators and provide a basis for consistent training of new operators. These procedures are periodically reviewed and annually certified as current and accurate. The procedures are kept current and accurate by revising them as necessary to reflect changes made through the management of change process. The operating procedures are centrally located and accessible to employees.   During storage, operator rounds are completed to ensure that the rail cars are not leaking. 

Training 
To complement the written procedures for process operations, the Verene Rail Load out facility has implemented a comprehensive training program for the employees involved in operating a process. New employees receive basic training in facility operations unless they provide written certification that they have the required knowledge, skills, and abilities to safely carry out their specific duties and responsibilities. Operations employees will undergo refresher training at least every three years. A training attendance record will be kept for training activities, and a verification of understanding will be conducted by a performance evaluation or through testing.

Maintenance 
The rail cars utilized at the facility are leased units and are not owned by MPLX. While the rail cars are present at the facility, MPLX personnel conduct visual inspections to ensure that the structural integrity of each rail car remains intact. These inspections are a critical part of the overall safety management system and help verify that the rail cars are in proper condition for use and storage.
Responsibility for the overall maintenance program and establishing the testing intervals for each rail car lies with the car owners. However, MPLX is responsible for inspecting and maintaining the valves on all rail cars each time a rail car enters the facility and before it departs. This process ensures that th

e rail car is safe for continued transport. All maintenance and inspection activities are completed in accordance with the requirements of CFR 173.31, adhering to federal regulations for the safe operation of rail cars.
Each rail car is clearly marked with information regarding the specific inspection and testing methods employed. For example, markings such as DOT-SP20820 and FRA-AIP 200203 are stamped on the rail cars to indicate compliance with applicable standards. The owner of the rail tank car is ultimately responsible for the completion of all required maintenance activities for the car, ensuring ongoing safety and regulatory compliance.

Incident Investigation 
MPLX promptly investigates incidents that resulted in, or reasonably could have resulted in, a fire/explosion, release, major property damage, environmental loss, or personal injury. The goal of each investigation is to determine the facts, determine what causal factors led to the incident and to develop corrective actions to prevent a recurrence of the incident or a similar incident. The investigation team consists of the immediate supervisor, one person knowledgeable in the process, and other members with appropriate experience to investigate and analyze the incident. The team documents its findings, develops recommendations to prevent a recurrence, and forwards these results to facility management for resolution. Corrective actions that are identified will be promptly addressed, resolved and tracked until they are completed. The final resolution of each finding or recommendation is documented, and the investigation results are reviewed with facility employees (including contractors) whose job tasks are relevant to the investigation. Incident investigation reports are retained for at least five years so that the reports can be reviewed during PHAs and PHA revalidations.?? 

Compliance Audits 
To help ensure compliance with the RMP, MPLX will periodically conduct an

audit to determine whether the procedures and practices required by the accident prevention program are being implemented. Compliance audits will be conducted at least every three years. Team membership will include at least one person knowledgeable of the system being audited. One member of the team must be qualified to lead the audit and be familiar with the auditing protocol being administered. The facility will maintain a listing of non-conformances identified during an audit and document closure of compliance audit action items. The two most recent audit reports will remain on file with the documentation of closed items.? 

Employee Participation
MPLX encourages employees to participate in the facets of process safety management and accident prevention. Examples of employee participation range from updating and compiling technical documents and chemical information to participating as a member of a hazard review team. Employees will be provided with the information created as part of the facility accident prevention program. Specific ways that employees can be involved in the accident prevention program are documented in an employee participation plan that is maintained at the facility. Company employees are encouraged to express their views concerning accident prevention issues and to recommend improvements.?

Emergency Response Program 
The Verne Railyard facility is a Non-Responding Facility as per 48 CFR 68.90(b).
The facility maintains a written emergency action plan, which is in place to help protect employees and public safety as well as the environment.  The plan identifies steps to be taken in case of an accidental release including evacuation plans, accounting for personnel after an evacuation, and notification of company staff, local emergency response agencies, and the public if a release occurs.  However, facility personnel are not trained to be first responders to large fires, and should a release occur from one of the railcars, the facility woul
d rely on the local fire department to respond.
